body.statement: For every \(0<r<\sqrt7/3\), \(0<|\delta|<1/8\), and \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)^{\prime}\) with \(\omega_2\ne0\), the law \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\). In score order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\), \[\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad b^{\star}(x)=\begin{pmatrix}\omega_1/2+xr\omega_2/2\\\omega_1/2-xr\omega_2/2\\\omega_2\end{pmatrix}.\] The conditional eigenvalues are \(3/8\) and \(3\{2\pm\sqrt{1+r^2}\}/16\), so the smallest exceeds \(1/8\). Both constant comparators equal \((\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)^{\prime}\), and \[\Delta(b^{\mathrm{OVS}})=\Delta(b^{\mathrm{const}})=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0.\] At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), the exact gain is \(3/512\).
body.justification: An open bounded family shows that the conditional gain is structural, not a singularity or one-law artifact.
body.gap: The banked parent exhibits a constant-covariate joint-loading gain; the sign-reversing binary mixture is the first construction in which every constant loading loses to covariate-adaptive weighting.
body.consumer: The family is the symbolic early-kill test for tangent exhaustion and a reproducible unit test for software implementation.
body.proof_tex:
The construction has \(p_{a,s}(x)=1/6\) for every \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x\in\{-1,1\}\), so overlap holds and \(\pi_{2,1}=1/6\).  The outcomes are bounded because \(|Z_t^{\mathrm w}|\le1/8\) and \(|\delta|<1/8\).  Consistency holds by construction.  When \(s=0\), the treatment term vanishes for every adoption date, proving no ineligible effect.  Before adoption the treatment term also vanishes, proving no anticipation pathwise for every retained cohort.  Finally, the law of \((U^{\mathrm w},V^{\mathrm w})\) depends on \((G,X)\) but not on \(S\).  Thus the never-enabled eligibility gap is zero in every cohort and period, which proves every conditional parallel-gap restriction.  Hence \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\in\mathcal M\).

The conditional means are
\[
m_{2,s,2}=s\delta,\quad m_{3,s,3}=s\delta,
\]
with every other retained one-step treatment term equal to zero.  Since \(E[U^{\mathrm w}\mid G,X]=E[V^{\mathrm w}\mid G,X]=0\), all three conditional DDD contrasts and both targets equal \(\delta\).  The corrected score therefore contains no residual categorical term proportional to \(\delta\).  Put \(a=3/4\).  In the declared score order, the nonzero residual values are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(G,S)&\Psi_{(2,2),3}&\Psi_{(2,2),\infty}&\Psi_{(2,3),\infty}\\ \hline
(2,1)&aU^{\mathrm w}&aU^{\mathrm w}&aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(2,0)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(3,1)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(3,0)&aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(\infty,1)&0&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(\infty,0)&0&aU^{\mathrm w}&aV^{\mathrm w}.
\end{array}
\]
Every row has conditional probability \(1/6\).  Also
\[
E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=2]=E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=3]=0,
\quad E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=\infty]=xr.
\]
Multiplying the entries row by row gives
\[
\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Feasibility is \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\), \(b_3=\omega_2\), so write
\[
b(q)=(\omega_1/2+q,\ \omega_1/2-q,\ \omega_2)'.
\]
Differentiating its conditional quadratic form gives
\[
\frac{d}{dq}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}=\frac{3}{16}\{4q-2xr\omega_2\}.
\]
The second derivative is \(3/4>0\), hence the unique optimum is \(q^\star(x)=xr\omega_2/2\), which yields the displayed \(b^\star(x)\).  The eigenvalues follow from
\[
\det\left\{\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix}-\lambda I\right\}
=(2-\lambda)\{(2-\lambda)^2-(1+r^2)\};
\]
they are \(2\) and \(2\pm\sqrt{1+r^2}\), multiplied by \(3/16\).  Since \(r^2<7/9\),
\[
\frac{3}{16}\{2-\sqrt{1+r^2}\}>\frac18.
\]

Because \(E[X]=0\), the unconditional covariance has its \((2,3)\) entry equal to zero.  The joint constant objective and the first OVS block are therefore uniquely minimized at \(q=0\), while the third coordinate is fixed; both named constant loadings equal \((\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)'\).  Their displacement from the conditional optimum is \((-xr\omega_2/2,xr\omega_2/2,0)'\).  Direct quadratic evaluation gives
\[
\Delta=E_P\left[\frac{3}{16}\,2\left(\frac{r\omega_2}{2}\right)^2\right]
=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0.
\]
At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), this is \(3/512\).  More generally, strict convexity shows that every constant \(q\ne0\) has still larger average loss, so the best constant itself already loses strictly.  In this particular architecture the only overidentifying restriction is the single period-two comparison between cohorts \(3\) and \(\infty\); its residual contrast is exactly \(N'R\).  Thus the period-specific and aggregate tangent-normal closures coincide here, so the general tangent-exhaustion defect does not invalidate this binary early-kill calculation.
